meta.one_line: The curated playground SET for 'A Duel Became a Crowd': ONE hero year-scrubber (the reader drags 1957->2018 and the two-superpower share falls under their hand from 99.2% to 46.3% while the per-country bars re-rank) + 5 supporting explorables, each bound to a DISTINCT finding and recomputed live on the Analyst's audited code/client_model.js so the in-browser number equals the published figure by construction.
meta.built_from: editor.json.interactives (hero ana_07 + ranked supporting[]); concepts from imagineer.json; design briefs des_08/des_10/des_12/des_13/des_17/des_20; recompute fns code/client_model.js (data slice code/client_data.json).
meta.node_verified: All recomputes were node-checked against code/client_model.js: launchSnapshot(1965)=99.2 / (2018)=46.3 ; cumulativeThrough(2018) old-world=85.5 ; annualize(28,10)=33.6 ; successRate('country','China')=95.7 ; ana_14 287/302=95.0 ; ana_15 first startup year=2006. No drift.
meta.ASSUMES_INLINED: The Programmer inlines code/client_model.js ONCE in the page <script> so launchSnapshot, cumulativeThrough, successRate, annualize and CLIENT_DATA are in global scope, and loads D3 (allowed CDN) for scales/joins/transitions. Each widget below is otherwise self-contained (any extra constants it needs are declared inside its own IIFE).

engine_preamble._note: Define these helpers ONCE near the top of the page <script>, before the per-widget IIFEs. Every widget reuses them. This is the universal_engine + the MANDATORY verify_coexistence guard + a reduced-motion + a country palette matching designer.json tokens.
js: const DUR = (ms) => reduced() ? 0 : (ms || 600);                                       // transition duration (override w/ motion.json --dur-* if wired)
engine_preamble.verify_coexistence_rule: EVERY mutating handler (slider input, button click, select change, play tick) MUST early-return `if (vOn()) return;` as its FIRST line, so under the Verify layer a gesture opens the provenance drawer instead of moving the readout. Do NOT guard render() itself (the baseline render must run). No feature handler may call stopPropagation (it must not eat the Verify click).
engine_preamble.control_floor: Every control (slider thumb, button, select) is a real, labelled, keyboard-operable native element with a >=44px hit-area and visible focus. Seed every control at the audited baseline so the untouched widget reproduces the published number.
engine_preamble.readout_floor: Every live readout exposes a BARE parseable number inside `<span class="po-num">` within the element carrying `data-play-out="int_NN"` (a NON-provenance hook). Units/labels live in sibling nodes, NOT inside .po-num, so the Playtester's recompute_oracle can parse the number.

centerpiece.reader_produces: Drag ONE year slider from 1957 to 2018 and watch the two-superpower (USA + USSR/Russia) combined share of that year's launches fall under your hand from 99.2% (1965, the duel) to 46.3% (2018, partial Jan-Oct, the crowd), while the per-country bars re-rank beneath it: a US/USSR duel -> Soviet dominance (1982: USSR 108 of 129) -> the 1991 collapse -> China taking the top bar in 2018. The reader produces the thesis ('a duel became a crowd') BEFORE the prose states it.
controls: range slider: year 1957-2018, step 1, seeded at 1965 (>=44px thumb, keyboard arrows, scroll-linked motion LINEAR)
button: '▶ Play' auto-advances the year 1957->2018 then stops (aria-pressed toggles; honors reduced-motion)
centerpiece.at_rest: Seeded at 1965: the big readout shows the bare duopoly share 99.2 (%) and the bars show USA 70 / USSR/Russia 53 towering over a near-empty field. 99.2 = launchSnapshot(1965).duopolyShare (audited).
centerpiece.on_interact: On slider 'input' (and on each Play tick): FIRST `if (vOn()) return;`, then state.year = +slider.value; render() calls launchSnapshot(year), writes duopolyShare into the .po-num node, re-ranks/resizes the per-country bars with a D3 join + transition, updates the leader label + the 'N countries launched this year' readout, and shows the PARTIAL badge when year===2018.
centerpiece.payoff: By 2018 the reader has produced, under their own hand, the duopoly share at 46.3% with China (28) topping the bars in the final partial year - the duel-became-a-crowd reveal is the reader's action, not the prose. The standfirst withheld the number; the scrubber hands it over.
centerpiece.placement: ABOVE the reveal paragraph in edt_03 (play-first: the slider is the first thing in the section, before any expository prose, so the reader manipulates immediately). The des_07 'how much is flat' area chart precedes the section; the prose reveal of the decade 54.5% follows the widget.
centerpiece.per_year_vs_decade_note: HONESTY GUARD for the Copywriter/Programmer/Auditor: this scrubber is PER-YEAR (launchSnapshot), so its 2018 endpoint is 46.3% (partial Jan-Oct) and its 1965 seed is 99.2%. The prose/standfirst headline 54.5% is the DECADE aggregate (ana_07 2010s row), a different granularity - NOT a contradiction. Label the widget readout explicitly 'of <year>'s launches' and mark 2018 partial; do NOT print '54.5%' as the scrubber's live value. Both numbers are audited and tell the same story (a duel became a crowd).
centerpiece.degradation: <noscript> (and JS-off): a static two-line statement - 'In 1965 the two superpowers launched 99.2% of the world's rockets. By 2018 (Jan-Oct, partial) just 46.3%, with China the single busiest launcher.' - plus the static des_04 stacked-area spine carries the same arc. Page still makes its point.
centerpiece.a11y: Native <input type=range> with <label for>, aria-valuetext echoing '<year>: duopoly <n>%'; native <button> Play with aria-pressed; bars are decorative SVG with the numbers also in the live text readouts (aria-live=polite on the readout block). Focus-visible on both controls; >=44px hit-areas.

supporting.reader_produces: Set how many months of 2018 the data covers and watch China's NAIVE full-year pro-rate move (28 -> 33.6 at 10 months) against the independent EXTERNAL full-year actual (39). At every honest granularity - partial (28>27), naive-annualized (33.6>32.4), external full-year (39>34) - China still leads. The reader verifies the 2018 crossover survives the truncation; this is the lead's credibility keystone.
controls: range slider: months elapsed 1-12, step 1, seeded at 10 (Jan-Oct, the dataset's real window) (>=44px thumb, keyboard); a 'reset to 10' affordance via the seed
supporting.inline_data_required: Constants NOT in client_model.js - inline from ana_19 data_table: PARTIAL = {China:28, USA:27, 'USSR/Russia':10}; EXTERNAL = {China:39, USA:34, 'USSR/Russia':20} (external full-year is an INDEPENDENT yardstick, never a model input).
supporting.at_rest: Seeded at monthsElapsed=10: China's naive projection = 33.6 in the .po-num; bars show, per country, the partial (fixed), the naive projection (recompute) and the external full-year ghost reference. 33.6 = annualize(28,10) (= published ana_19 naive_annualized).
supporting.on_interact: On slider 'input': FIRST `if (vOn()) return;`, then state.months=+slider.value; render() recomputes annualize(PARTIAL[c], months) per country, rewrites China's projection into .po-num, and redraws the projection bars as a DELTA against the FIXED external full-year reference (the 39/34/20 stay constant - do not recompute them from the slider).
supporting.payoff: However the reader sets the months, China stays ahead - the crossover is not a truncation artifact. HONEST framing rendered on the widget: this is a naive linear pro-rate, NOT a forecast, and it validates a per-year COUNT, not 'China owns space'.
supporting.degradation: <noscript>/JS-off: static text - 'At 10 months, China's 28 projects to ~33.6 for the full year (naive x12/10), vs an external actual of 39. China leads at partial (28>27), annualized (33.6>32.4) and full-year (39>34).'
supporting.a11y: Native range + label + aria-valuetext '<n> months: China ~<proj>'; aria-live=polite on the readout; the 'naive pro-rate, not a forecast' caption is real text. >=44px, focus-visible.

supporting.reader_produces: Guess what share of China's 302 launches were a single rocket family, commit it, then meet the data-bound correction: 287 of 302 = 95.0% were Long March (Chang Zheng). China's rise IS one sovereign rocket family scaling up - unlike the diversified US fleet (Thor/Delta, Atlas, Titan, Shuttle, Falcon).
controls: range slider: your guess 0-100% (>=44px thumb, keyboard), live echo of the guess
supporting.inline_data_required: From ana_14 data_table: {longMarch:287, total:302}. The REAL value is computed data-bound = 100*287/302 -> 95.0 (NEVER a hardcoded bar width).
supporting.at_rest: Guess slider at 50% with a live echo; the answer track is empty/hidden. The .po-num holds the real Long March share, populated on Reveal (95.0).
supporting.on_interact: Slider 'input': FIRST `if (vOn()) return;`, then update the guess echo. Reveal 'click': FIRST `if (vOn()) return;`, then draw BOTH bars from data - your guess vs the real 95.0 (computed from the inlined 287/302 on a 0-100 D3 scale, animated in) - write 95.0 into .po-num, and branch a one-line verdict off the signed gap (over/under/close).
supporting.payoff: The concentration lands as a felt correction: nearly the whole Chinese program is one family. Distinct from the country-count story (it is about ONE family, not many countries).
supporting.degradation: <noscript>/JS-off: static text + the static des_09 China decade-ramp column nearby - '287 of 302 (95.0%) of China's launches were the Long March family.'
supporting.a11y: Native range + label + aria-valuetext '<guess>%'; native Reveal <button>; aria-live=polite on the reveal/readout. >=44px, focus-visible.

supporting.payoff: The reader feels how RECENT and how steep the venture wave is - one firm launching at a mid-size national rate by 2018 - a producible finding no country widget covers.

transitions: int_01 / int_02 bars: D3 horizontal-bar join with .transition().duration(DUR(600-700)).ease(easeCubicOut) on re-rank + resize (never hard pops); count text set on transition 'start'.

ALL scroll-linked / slider-dragged motion is LINEAR (no easing on the scrub itself); easing applies only to the discrete re-render transitions. Drive durations from motion.json --dur-* tokens if the Programmer has them wired; otherwise the DUR() helper above.
